Edit: Let the record show that I do live in Dallas. I have a local guide badge. Since you went through my review history, you're aware of that. In fact, I live within a short driving distance of your location and am willing to visit again, if you'd like, to give a "fair" review. Below will show proof of the fact I live here. Reviewing my history, you're also aware of the fact that I have left reviews without comment before. You can visit a place and review it later, even if the business is closed. You can also review businesses based on publicly available information, especially whenever you ship these animals and are not solely based in the Dallas area because of this fact. Don't own a business if you can't handle negative reviews. I didn't want to comment because that's my right, but since you want to be sassy, let me put my thoughts.

In my opinion, this place is the axolotl equivalent of a puppy mill. The tanks are depressing. Axolotls don't have eyelids and need adequate shelter from light - there is nothing in their tanks at all. I understand axolotls can eat things they shouldn't. That's when you put plants or tank safe objects that are too large for them to ingest. Axolotls should not be pets to begin with. They are a critically endangered species.

You're welcome. I hope you know what to make of this now. 😊

Edit 2: I don't agree with you or your contradicting points lol. Simple as that. I could respond point by point but I'm not going to, considering Google reviews are meant to be simple and reflect my opinion. They aren't debate stages. I'm going to point out the most glaring inconsistencies though.

You say the bare tanks are intentional because enrichment objects can compromise water quality, but then you say you maintain a fully enriched model habitat and encourage customers to recreate it. So do axolotls need appropriate habitat features or not? Because your answer changes depending on which part of the criticism you’re responding to.

Not to mention you completely skated around my point about axolotls being a critically endangered species that belong in the wild. The irony of you saying this isn't like a puppy mill after stating you've handled over 10,000 axolotls too. That is certainly not at all helping you beat the volume-based breeding claims. Just saying. Put simply, I believe what you do is unethical and I'm not a fan.

Hi there! Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback here. Can we ask if there was something specific you encountered with us that resulted in this review?

I do not generally write reviews and I truly try to give everyone the benefit of the doubt. I went out of my way and drove 2 hours specifically to come to this store. I had a meeting prior and came here once it was over to look at the selection that they had. I personally have an Axolotl of my own and was originally coming to see if they had a variety of food options or cool morphs to look at. We were greeted and everything seemed to go well at first. We did chit chat with the gentleman that was working there a bit, and as an experienced aquarium enthusiast myself it’s always awesome to speak with other people about the hobby! My experience started to shift when the gentleman working noticed a baby axo cannibalizing the other and his immediate response was “eh it’ll grow back” and “it’s been hard to keep them fed with the holiday rush” after this I asked if there were any leucistics in larger sizes. I walked over to a tank that had some babies in it and instead of answering my question he started going on about how those in that tank were from a local breeder who he isn’t to keen on. He described how much he didn’t like her and how he has much more of a success rate than her and how his look better etc etc. My parter and I looked at each other in disbelief. To attempt to tone down the conversation I mentioned how I know breeding these guys can be a process as I used to several years ago. I mentioned that I had an axo of my own at home and was going to pick up two rescued females tomorrow from a friend. I noticed that some of their new arrivals had laid eggs and mentioned that I was curious to see if the rescued females would lay eggs once I introduced them to their forever tanks bc water parameters would be different, I was attempting to make conversation and relate since my two rescues would also be new intakes. I the walked over to their coppers and asked if I could get one. Without hesitation the gentleman said “I cannot sell them to you since you’re a breeder.” I was in genuine shock bc nowhere did I mention to him that I was breeding axolotls in todays day in age. I mentioned that I used to back in 2017 but did not have any plans of it as I have a full time job and absolutely zero time in my day to raise them anymore. I had to pull out my phone and show him text messages between my friend and I discussing that I had no intentions on breeding them alongside the time stamps of when they were sent so he new that I wasn’t lying? He then became combative and stating that it wasn’t his intention to be rude. The whole conversation about breeding axolotls came up as a de escalation conversation when he was bragging about his axos being better than one of their vendors. The store was a little confusing with the labeling and majority of their stock was either NFS or being treated for disease. It was hard to tell which ones were for sale and which weren’t. What could have been a wonderful experience turned into one of the most awkward, frustrating, and embarrassing experiences of my life. I do not know if I will ever be back.
